open_points.subject: Project and Customer revision — which actions move it
open_points.text: every accepted change moves by one. A change names the revision it was made
open_points.question: Which accepted changes move the revision? The last-changed instant is enumerated action by action, the revision is not. Does archiving, adding a room, publishing or withdrawing a pointer, a session grant, restricting/lifting, ending/resuming or erasing move the revision, and must those actions state a revision (State 0 lists a stale-revision refusal only for 'correct a project' and 'correct a customer')?
options: revision moves exactly when the last-changed instant moves
revision moves on every accepted write including archive, room add, marks and erasure
revision moves only on 'correct' actions
open_points.default_guess: revision moves exactly when the last-changed instant moves; only 'correct' actions must state one

open_points.subject: Project last-changed instant — stored or derived
open_points.text: Written once, derived and not a fact of its own: the last-changed instant
open_points.question: A last-changed instant that moves on every correction cannot be 'written once'; and if it is 'derived', from what — the audit log (which the owner may erase by date, R0-66) or the record itself? Is it a stored fact of the Project or computed?
options: stored on the record, rewritten by each change
derived from the latest audit entry
derived from the revision history
open_points.default_guess: stored on the record, rewritten by each change; drop 'written once'

open_points.subject: What an anonymised project keeps
open_points.text: it keeps its `project_id`, its status, its archived instant and its
open_points.question: The lifecycle text keeps id, status, archived instant and pointers 'and nothing else'; the Open questions add the anonymised instant; the facts list the anonymised mark and a created instant. Exactly which of created instant, anonymised instant, anonymised mark and last-changed instant survive anonymisation?
options: id, status, archived instant, anonymised instant and mark, pointers; created and last-changed gone
the above plus the created instant
everything time-related kept, only name/alias/object/customer/rooms/revision gone
open_points.default_guess: id, status, created instant, archived instant, anonymised instant and mark, pointers; revision and last-changed gone

open_points.subject: Times and revision of imported records
open_points.text: record carries the instant it was created and the instant it was last
open_points.question: For projects, customers, rooms and pointers the import brings in, are the created, last-changed, archived and published instants kept from the VPS record or set to the import instant? Does an imported project's revision start at 1 or carry the v1 value? Does an imported archived project get an archived date when v1 has none?
options: all instants kept from the source, revision restarts at 1
all instants set at import, revision 1
instants kept where the source has them, else the import instant
open_points.default_guess: instants kept where the source has them, else the import instant; revision 1

open_points.subject: Identity format left open to the owner
open_points.text: the owner may choose otherwise, and the import then maps v1
open_points.question: Is the UUID format decided or not? R0-79 imports the two projects 'under the ids Client Portal already names', so a mapping of v1 ids contradicts State 0. Which is it: UUID fixed and v1 ids kept verbatim, or a format still open with a mapping the import performs?
options: UUID fixed, v1 ids kept verbatim, no mapping
format open, import maps and consumers relink
open_points.default_guess: UUID fixed, v1 ids kept verbatim; strike the mapping clause

open_points.subject: What an erased Customer keeps
open_points.text: the Customer keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased; name, phone, e-mail and language are gone; projects still name it (R0-06)
open_points.question: State 0 says only identity and the erased fact survive and names only contact data as gone; State 1 M04 keeps also the kind, the revision, the recorded instant and the restricted/ended marks with their dates, and erases tax id and legal name too. Which facts of an erased Customer survive, and are fiscal values erased with the contact data?
options: identity + erased mark + instant only
identity, kind, erased mark/instant, restricted/ended marks, revision; fiscal data gone
identity, kind, erased mark; fiscal data kept for issued-document purposes
open_points.default_guess: identity, kind, erased mark and instant, other marks kept; contact and fiscal data gone

open_points.subject: The Customer the import makes from a v1 customer_ref
open_points.text: a v1 `customer_ref` that is not a Registry-minted id becomes a new Customer with a minted `customer_ref`, the old value moving to its tax id when it is one, and its projects are linked to that Customer (R0-80)
open_points.question: Which kind (person/company) does this Customer get, when 'record a customer' refuses a missing kind? Where does the v1 value go when it is not a tax id — dropped, or kept as name? How does the import tell a 'Registry-minted' customer_ref from a v1 value — by UUID shape? Does the VPS export carry Customer records with contact data at all, or only the string on the project? And may a Customer with an absent name exist and be listed, when recording one refuses a missing name?
options: kind required at import from the owner per customer
kind defaulted to person
kind absent until the owner corrects it
open_points.default_guess: the owner gives kind (and name) per customer at import time; a non-tax-id value is dropped; minted means UUID-shaped

open_points.subject: Marks with a context-dependent class
open_points.text: the end-of-relationship date and the restriction mark where they are read together with a customer's name
open_points.question: A field is given two classes depending on the answer it appears in. Is each field's class fixed (the mark and date business_confidential, the answer's class raised by the name beside it), or do these fields carry personal_data as fields? The same question applies to the ended date of an erased Customer, which has no name beside it.
options: mark and date are business_confidential; the answer's class is the highest of its fields
mark and date are personal_data always
open_points.default_guess: mark and date are business_confidential; the answer's class is the highest of its fields

open_points.subject: Fields missing from the class table
open_points.text: `room_id` and room name; every artifact pointer field; every agent session fact; every audit entry
open_points.question: The table omits: a Room's added instant and acting principal (M03), the Customer's revision, recorded and last-changed instants, the Project's anonymised instant, every fact of MigrationClosure (M10) and OwnerSession (M11), and the AccessRequest text. What class does each carry?
options: all business_confidential
AccessRequest text personal_data because it may name a person
open_points.default_guess: all business_confidential, the request text under the writer rule like room names

open_points.subject: Which actions create an audit entry
open_points.text: change to a project or a customer record, a grant or revocation of a session's
open_points.question: Is adding a room, publishing or withdrawing a pointer, registering a session, an access request, changing or clearing the active project, ending/resuming a relationship, correcting fiscal data, and the import itself a 'significant change of state' that writes an entry? What is the subject of the import's entry (many projects) and of the dated erasure (none)?
options: only the actions R0-58 names literally
every owner or service write except reads
every write except access requests and session registration
open_points.default_guess: every accepted write that changes a record, with room add and pointer publish included and session registration/request excluded; the import's subject is the closure digest

open_points.subject: Identity of an audit entry
open_points.text: Substitution: two entries with equal facts are two events
open_points.question: M09 is an entity but lists no identity fact. Does Registry mint an entry id, and who reads it (the erasure by date needs none)?
options: Registry mints an opaque id per entry
no id; position in time order is its identity
open_points.default_guess: Registry mints an opaque id per entry

open_points.subject: Confirmation id — who mints it
open_points.text: the confirmation id where the owner confirmed (R0-37);
open_points.question: M09 and M10 record a confirmation id, but no model mints it and no action creates it. Is it minted by Registry when the owner interface asks for confirmation (a record of its own or an OwnerSession fact), supplied by the interface, or the audit entry's own id?
options: Registry mints it at the confirmation step as a value in the OwnerSession
it is the audit entry's own id
the owner interface supplies it
open_points.default_guess: Registry mints it at the confirmation step; it is not a durable model

open_points.subject: Access version — stated then deferred
open_points.text: None for identity. The access version's start and what moves it are State 2's
open_points.question: The facts list says the version moves on every change of the granted set, the active project or the pending request; the Open questions say what moves it is State 2's. Is the facts statement a State 1 decision (so archiving a granted project, which changes nothing in the set, does not move it; the project's erasure does)?
options: facts statement is binding; State 2 only sets the starting value
entirely State 2
open_points.default_guess: facts statement is binding; State 2 sets the start

open_points.subject: Repeated equal request
open_points.text: pending request is whichever was made last; two equal texts in one session are
open_points.question: If a session re-sends the same text, is the pending request's 'made' instant rewritten and does the session's access version move, or is nothing changed because it is 'the same pending request'?
options: replaced: new instant, version moves
unchanged: same instant, version does not move

open_points.subject: Object kind — vocabulary or free text
open_points.text: Facts: address (required); kind; the declared characteristics (their list is
open_points.question: Is the object's kind a closed vocabulary the specification declares (it is absent from 'Declared vocabularies') or free text the owner writes? Is it required at creation like the address?
options: declared enum (e.g. flat, house, building, premises)
free text
optional free text
open_points.default_guess: a declared vocabulary, optional at creation

open_points.subject: Erasure and the other marks
open_points.text: restricted and ended at once; erasure does not clear the other marks (what it
open_points.question: The lifecycle says what erasure does to the marks 'is settled in State 2 if anything', while the Open questions say it is settled: 'erasure clears none of them'. State 0 refuses restrict/lift and end/resume on an erased customer, so a mark set before erasure can never be lifted. Is that the intended final state?
options: settled: marks survive erasure and are frozen
erasure clears both marks
State 2 decides
open_points.default_guess: settled: marks survive and are frozen

open_points.subject: Room's acting principal — new fact against State 0
open_points.text: Facts: `room_id`, minted by Registry or kept by the import; its name, as its
open_points.question: State 0's 'add a room' output is id, name and project; State 1 adds the instant and the acting principal. For imported rooms, which principal is recorded (owner as importer, or none)? Does the agent projection or 'list rooms' expose the principal to Kernel?
options: owner for imported rooms; principal in owner reads only
principal absent for imported rooms
principal exposed in every room list
open_points.default_guess: owner for imported rooms; the principal is read by the owner only
